findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py (diff ~L504-515): `frozenset(k for k in args.kinds.split(",") if k)` goes straight into WorkerContext with no check against the known job kinds. The spec says an unevaluable condition SHALL refuse. The `work-next` path does validate kinds elsewhere.
findings.summary: `worker-preflight` accepts any `--kinds` string. A typo such as `reveiw` makes every condition not-applicable, and the command exits 0 as if the environment were proven.

findings.evidence: scripts/post_merge_runner.py adds `ENVIRONMENT_EXIT = 3  # lifecycle_workers.ENVIRONMENT_EXIT`. tests/test_worker_preflight.py::RunnerTests only greps the source text for the literal. A different failure that also exits 3 would be recorded as outcome "environment" and end the round with no job-failure accounting.
findings.summary: `ENVIRONMENT_EXIT = 3` is hand-copied into scripts/post_merge_runner.py. Exit 3 is also the only signal the runner uses to tell an environment stop from a job failure.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py:849-859: `active_gh_token` raises only for the failed `gh auth token`. The decorator wraps all `WorkerError`s, so any WorkerError added later would be released as environment, outside MAX_RELEASES, with a bound of 5.
findings.summary: `@environment_condition("github-credential")` turns every `WorkerError` from `active_gh_token` into a free-of-charge EnvironmentFailure. That is safe today only because the function has a single raise site.
